title: Practice: diagnose a failure from a trace (TypeScript)

cases.id: m1 each documented http error maps to a type an origin and a recovery
cases.says: Each documented HTTP error maps to its type, origin and recovery

cases.id: e1 a 429 is a rate limit or a spend cap and other statuses fall back by class
cases.says: The two kinds of 429, the 400 spend limit, and the fallback by class for statuses the table does not list

cases.id: e2 a successful response can still fail by its stop reason
cases.says: A 200 response with a failing stop reason, and the stop reasons that are fine

cases.id: e3 an empty end turn is the integration when text followed the tool result and the model otherwise
cases.says: An empty end_turn: our message structure or the model, by the last user message's blocks

cases.id: e4 a parse failure is the integration when a json object is in the text and the model when not
cases.says: A parse failure: our parser or the model, by whether a JSON object is in the text

cases.id: e5 tool failures split into a model that called a missing tool and our tool that raised
cases.says: A tool name the model invented against our own tool raising; a tool-reported error is not a failure

cases.id: e6 the first failure names the cause and a later good response marks it recovered
cases.says: The first failure wins, with its index; a later good response means it recovered; a clean or empty trace is ok

cases.id: e7 a dropped connection has no status and belongs to the service side
cases.says: A dropped connection has no status and belongs to the service side, and may recover
